title: AI Is Making Content Cheaper. That Could Make Human Creativity More Valuable
tldr: As AI floods the internet with cheap content, human creativity, taste and point of view become the scarce differentiator. A core thesis for anyone betting on human-centered content.
angle: Write about why 'taste' and human judgment are the last defensible moat in an AI-content economy.

title: The Only Two Types of Content that AI Can Never Make
tldr: Orbit Media argues original research and firsthand experience are the two content types AI structurally cannot produce, making them strategic priorities. Concrete and actionable for content strategists.
angle: Build a content pillar strategy around 'AI-proof' formats: original data and lived experience.

title: The myth of the changing consumer
tldr: Argues that 'the consumer has changed' is usually lazy shorthand and that real insight comes from context behind the trend. A useful corrective for anyone chasing media-consumption fads.
angle: Write a myth-busting piece on how brands misread 'changing behavior' when the context, not the person, shifted.

title: AI Traffic Conversion Rates: New Research from 97 B2B Websites and 29M visits
tldr: Fresh proprietary research on how visitors arriving from AI search actually convert versus traditional search. Rare hard data on the AI-discovery shift.
angle: Analyze what AI-referral conversion data means for content attribution models.

title: The Library Newsroom Project could be coming to a library near you
tldr: A push to rebuild local journalism inside libraries, meeting people 'where they actually live their lives.' A striking human-centered rethink of news distribution.
angle: Explore physical, community-rooted content distribution as an antidote to platform dependence.

title: Dentsu taps microdrama trend for Co-op
tldr: Co-op launches its first microdrama with Dentsu, prompting the question of whether it's a genuinely new format or a relabelled soap ad. A concrete campaign breakdown around short-form video.
angle: Dissect microdramas: real new storytelling format or repackaged serialized advertising?

title: Workforce Media Platforms Ranked for Brand Locked Employee Content
tldr: A ranking of platforms built specifically for brand-governed employee-generated content. Directly relevant to EGC and content governance at scale.
angle: Map the emerging tooling for scaling employee-generated content without losing brand governance.

title: Meta streamlines creator, brand tie-ups with new marketing hub
tldr: Meta adds a hub with ad-readiness editing and expanded APIs to help advertisers find and work with creators. A platform shift shaping the creator-brand pipeline.
angle: Assess how platform-native creator marketplaces reshape brand-creator collaboration.

title: AI Agents Are the New Gatekeepers
tldr: Gini Dietrich argues AI agents are becoming the gatekeepers of brand visibility—and no ad budget can buy your way in. A provocative framing of the AEO/discovery shift.
angle: Explore what it means for PR when AI agents, not editors or algorithms, decide brand visibility.

title: Colleges mark back to school with new creator programs
tldr: Universities are launching formal creator-economy programs to train students as content creators. Signals institutionalization of the creator career path.
angle: Write about the creator economy going academic and what it means for talent pipelines.

title: Bots Don't Click — So What Will The Internet's New Business Model Be?
tldr: As AI agents replace human clicks, the ad-and-traffic-based web economy faces collapse. A big-picture challenge to how content gets funded.
angle: Speculate on content business models in a world where AI agents, not humans, consume the web.

title: Axios preps new Axios Direct feeds for AI models, agents as revenue tops 2026 goal
tldr: Axios builds a new revenue stream feeding content directly to AI models and agents. A publisher actively monetizing the AI-consumption shift.
angle: Break down licensing content to AI as an emerging owned-media revenue play.

title: How Rob Farmer turns half-baked sketches into New York Times covers
tldr: A motion designer explains procedural workflows, editorial deadlines and why perfectionism blocks good work getting seen. A candid craft-and-process case study.
angle: Use his 'perfectionism is the enemy' ethos to argue for shipping over polishing in content ops.

title: What Your Marketing and Communications Measurement is Missing
tldr: Argues measurement should capture trust, reputation and relationships—not just revenue. A useful reframe for comms metrics beyond attribution.
angle: Propose a measurement model that quantifies trust and reputation alongside ROI.
